sense: a model author of the first rank

terms.comment: Gellius’s figure from the census: the classicī were citizens of the first class, so a classicus scrīptor is a first-class writer, set against a prōlētārius, one of the lowest. Elsewhere classicus means “of the fleet”, as classicī mīlitēs, marines (Liv. 21.61.2). In modern Latin it is also “classical”, of Greek and Roman antiquity (Vives; M-O).

terms.gloss: an author, a writer whose word carries weight
evidence: Cic. Att. 12.18: iī quōs nunc lēctitō auctōrēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The writer of a work, and the authority one follows; the word for the authors one reads as models. First of all the originator or founder of anything (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: id est classicus adsiduusque aliquis scrīptor, nōn prōlētārius
phrases.english: that is, some classic writer of standing, not one of the rabble
the classics (the great authors of Greek and Latin)
